question: If u, g, and h are the initial velocity, gravitational acceleration, and height, respectively, of an object falling under gravitational force, then its final velocity v can be obtained from:
solution:
The correct answer is __**v² - u² = 2gh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The equation **v² - u² = 2gh** is derived from the kinematic equations of motion, which are fundamental in physics for describing the motion of objects.
 
• In this context, **u** represents the initial velocity of the object, **v** is the final velocity, **g** is the acceleration due to gravity, and **h** is the height from which the object falls.
 
• This equation assumes that the only force acting on the object is gravity, meaning air resistance and other forces are negligible.
 
• The formula is particularly useful for calculating the final velocity of an object in free fall when the initial velocity and height are known.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinematic Equations:**

 
 
• These are equations that describe the motion of objects without considering the causes of the motion.
 
• They are crucial in solving problems related to uniformly accelerated motion.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• The standard value of gravitational acceleration on Earth is approximately 9.81 m/s².
 
• It is a constant that is used in various calculations involving free-falling objects.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• It is the motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.
 
• In a vacuum, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass.
 
 
 
• **Initial and Final Velocity:**
 
 
• Initial velocity (u) is the velocity of the object before it starts falling.
 
• Final velocity (v) is the velocity of the object just before it hits the ground or stops accelerating.
